facts.fact: bpy.data.curves.new(name, 'CURVE') makes curve data that is 2D (dimensions '2D'), resolution_u 12, no bevel
splines.new('BEZIER') starts with 1 bezier point; add more with bezier_points.add(n)
handle types; AUTO handles are computed when the curve is evaluated
a 2D curve keeps its points' z when evaluated (the 2D flag changes the fill and bevel options, and the fill_mode default is 'NONE' until set to 3D, where it becomes 'FULL')
an open bezier with 4 points and resolution_u 12 becomes 37 vertices / 36 edges with no faces
bevel_depth 0.1 sweeps a round profile along it; open ends stay open unless use_fill_caps
use_fill_caps closes the ends (but the result is still not manifold: cap vertices are separate from the tube)
bevel_mode 'OBJECT' with a closed square poly curve as bevel_object sweeps a square tube
POLY/NURBS spline points have 4D co (x, y, z, w); assigning a 3-tuple raises
facts.error: ValueError: bpy_struct: item.attr = val: sequences of dimension 0 should contain 4 items, not 3

facts.fact: a closed 10-point POLY circle evaluates to 10 verts and 10 edges (resolution does not apply to poly)
2D curve with fill_mode BOTH fills the closed shape with faces
new_from_object(evaluated curve object) gives a mesh datablock of the evaluated curve
bpy.ops.object.convert(target='MESH') works headless with an override and replaces the curve object's data with a mesh
